days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start beneath Neuschwanstein Castle and follow the Deutsche Alpenstraße through the Bavarian foothills. The route combines smooth sweepers, forested climbs, lakeside bends and frequent village sections, with generally excellent pavement and moderate tourist traffic. 
The approach to Walchensee is especially rewarding, with clear water, high ridges and well-surfaced mountain roads. Expect coaches, cyclists and camper vans around the most popular viewpoints, particularly during summer weekends.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east through the Bavarian pre-Alps on a mixture of regional roads and quieter connecting sections. The route passes forests, farmland and lake country, with broad curves and smooth surfaces that allow a relaxed touring rhythm. 
Continue toward Berchtesgaden. Traffic increases near larger towns and resort areas, but the road remains scenic and logically connected, giving you long mountain views before the overnight stop.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Start in Berchtesgaden and visit Eagle’s Nest / Kehlsteinhaus before climbing the Roßfeld Panoramastraße. Access to Kehlsteinhaus is via the Obersalzberg shuttle bus and lift; motorcycles remain at the designated parking area. The Roßfeld road offers broad bends, open alpine slopes and panoramic viewpoints, making it one of Germany’s finest motorcycle roads. 
Descend through Ramsau and Hintersee, then finish beside the emerald water of Königssee. The final roads are slower, with visitors and buses around the lake, but the scenery creates an ideal end to this three-day Bavarian route.

title: IT01 — Garda, Iseo and Como Lakes Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Italy

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start on Strada della Forra, the cliff-cut road above Lake Garda with tunnels, rock walls and dramatic views down to the water. Continue through Tremosine and Limone sul Garda, where the roads stay close to the lake and the villages feel like part of the landscape rather than separate from it. 
The day is compact but technical, with narrow sections, tourist traffic and frequent photo stops. Pavement is generally good, though the gorge and lake roads can be busy in peak season.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride from Lake Garda toward Lake Iseo, then take the ferry to Monte Isola. The crossing is an essential part of the route, and the island’s fishing villages give the day a slower, more local character. 
Continue to Lovere for the overnight stop. Roads around Iseo are smooth but busy near the popular lakeshores, and ferry timings should be checked in advance so the route remains realistic.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Finish through Lake Como with Bellagio and Varenna, where the roads are narrow, scenic and often slower because of traffic and village geometry. This part of the route is more about atmosphere than speed, with villas, ferries and steep lakeside slopes. 
Stop at Mandello del Lario to include the Moto Guzzi connection before wrapping up the loop. Expect heavy tourist use on the Como shoreline, especially in summer and around the main towns.

title: SI01 — Julian Alps and Soča Valley Loop
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Slovenia

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Kranjska Gora, with a food stop at Brunarica Kosobrin, then climb Vršič Pass. The road is defined by its 50 hairpins, steep gradients and cobbled sections, making it one of the most iconic mountain roads in the Julian Alps. 
Descend into the Soča Valley toward Bovec. The scenery is spectacular and the riding is technical enough to stay engaging, but the narrow road and changing weather require careful attention.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Visit Fort Kluže and then climb Mangart Saddle Road, Slovenia’s highest paved road. The route is short in distance but highly concentrated in difficulty, with narrow lanes, exposed sections and dramatic alpine scenery. 
Continue toward Bled via the northern Alpine corridors. The road becomes more open as you leave the high mountain zone, but the scenery remains strong and the driving stays scenic and flowing.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Return via the Julian Alpine ring, linking the turquoise Soča corridor back to Kranjska Gora. The roads are a blend of fast valley stretches and tighter mountain bends, with excellent pavement and frequent places to stop. 
Weather can shift quickly in the high country, and tourist traffic is common near the most famous viewpoints. It is a strong final day that ties together the route’s alpine valleys, mountain passes and blue rivers.

title: GR01 — Wild Crete Mountain and South Coast Route
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Greece

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Chania through Therisso Gorge, where the road narrows between the White Mountains and the ride immediately becomes more technical. Continue to Omalos Plateau and use the Samaria Gorge trailhead at Xyloskalo as a scenic point and optional walking stop. 
There is no through road for cars or motorcycles across Samaria Gorge, so the route does not enter or pass through the gorge. After the stop near Omalos, continue the next riding stage toward Askifou and the southern coast.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue from Omalos across Askifou and descend through Imbros Gorge, which gives the route its most concentrated series of switchbacks. The road is narrow, scenic and very much a mountain route rather than a simple cross-island connector. 
Finish at Chora Sfakion on the Libyan Sea. Traffic is light away from the main villages, but the gorge can be sensitive to loose stones and changing weather, especially in shoulder seasons.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride the south coast past Frangokastello and Preveli, combining sea-level curves with short inland connectors. The landscape is drier and more open here, and the road feels remote even when the coastline is close. 
The final run to Rethymno is more straightforward, but the mix of fortress, monastery and beach scenery keeps the day varied. Expect summer heat, wind exposure and occasional tourist traffic near the major coastal stops.

title: FI01 — Arctic Circle to Utsjoki Lapland Ride
subtitle: A 4-day tour of Finland

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Rovaniemi and head north on the E75 before turning toward Torvinen and Route 962. Continue through Pyhä-Luosto National Park and onward to Sodankylä, where the urban landscape gives way to endless forests, fells and empty northern roads. 
The roads are generally wide, smooth and easy to follow, but distances between services increase quickly. Reindeer can appear suddenly on the asphalt, particularly in the early morning and evening, while weather may change rapidly even in summer.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue north through Tankavaara and Saariselkä toward Lake Inari and the village of Inari. The route passes through taiga, open fells and long stretches with almost no traffic, creating the vast northern atmosphere that defines Finnish Lapland. 
Fuel and food stops should be planned in advance, especially before leaving Saariselkä. The riding is not technically difficult, but monotony, wind, wildlife and large distances require consistent concentration.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Leave Inari and continue through Kaamanen toward Utsjoki and Nuorgam, the northernmost village in Finland. The road follows wide river valleys and open Arctic terrain, with treeless fells and increasingly remote landscapes along the Teno River. 
The route remains mostly smooth and flowing, but services are limited and temperatures can drop quickly. Keep the fuel tank topped up and watch carefully for reindeer, especially on open sections with long sightlines.

days.title: Day 4
days.description:
Finish with a scenic ride from Nuorgam along the Teno River back to Utsjoki. The route offers open Arctic landscapes, low fells, sparse settlements and a powerful sense of distance from the rest of Europe. 
This final stage brings the complete route to approximately 940 kilometres over four days. Nordkapp remains an optional continuation from Utsjoki into Norway for riders who want to extend the northern journey.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Cluj-Napoca and head into the Apuseni Mountains through forests and traditional villages. The road gradually tightens and climbs, with a rural feel that is very different from Romania’s famous headline passes. 
Reach Padiș Plateau and Belvedere Glăvoaia, where the scenery opens up to forested ridges and wide mountain views. Road quality is variable on smaller sections, so expect patched surfaces and occasional gravel.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue toward Cheile Turzii and Rimetea, where limestone walls and narrow valley roads create the route’s most dramatic scenery. The ride is still accessible, but the road surface can change quickly in forested and canyon sections. 
Finish in Alba Iulia at the Alba Carolina fortress. The day combines mountain riding with a more historic urban finish, and traffic increases as you leave the highland roads behind.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Use the final day to return through Turda Gorge and back to Cluj-Napoca. This is a more direct riding day, with smoother regional roads and fewer major elevation changes than the previous stages. 
The gorge and surrounding countryside still give the route a scenic finish, but the final leg is best treated as a practical return rather than a technical highlight. Fuel and service availability improve as you approach the city.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Glencoe and follow the A82 to Fort William before heading west through Glenfinnan and down to Mallaig. The roads are classic Highland touring: broad scenery, fast-changing weather and a mixture of A-road flow and narrower coastal approaches. 
The section to Mallaig is especially good in clear weather, but coaches, camper vans and tourist traffic are common. Ferry reservations should be checked before departure if you are continuing to Skye.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Take the ferry from Mallaig to the Isle of Skye, then ride toward the Quiraing and Neist Point. The roads are narrow, scenic and often slow because of single-track sections, passing places and tourist vehicles. 
Skye’s weather can change quickly, and wind exposure is common on the west coast. The day is less about speed and more about constant scenery and careful, patient riding.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Leave Skye and head for Bealach na Bà, one of the most demanding and famous roads in the Highlands. The climb is steep, narrow and exposed, with hairpins and limited visibility that make it unsuitable for inexperienced riders in poor weather. 
Continue through Applecross and Torridon to Ullapool on some of Scotland’s best coastal and mountain roads. Expect single-track sections, livestock, rain, and very limited opportunities to overtake safely.

title: NL01 — North Sea, Texel and Friesland Dike Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Netherlands

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Ride from Alkmaar to the North Sea coast at Bergen aan Zee, then continue to Den Helder for the ferry to Texel. The riding is flat and easy, but wind, sand and busy coastal traffic are the main factors to watch. 
Explore Texel after the ferry, where the roads through the dunes are quiet and scenic. Because the route depends on ferry times, it is worth planning the day so you are not caught waiting at the harbor.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Cross back to the mainland and ride over the Afsluitdijk, one of the most distinctive long crossings in the Netherlands. The road is straight, exposed and very dependent on weather, especially crosswinds. 
Continue to Harlingen for the overnight stop. The route is technically simple, but the dike roads, open horizon and water on both sides give it a strong touring identity.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride through the Friesland dike network and fishing villages toward Lauwersmeer. The roads are flat and easy, with narrow shoulders and frequent water views. 
The final stage is more about rhythm and landscape than technical riding. Expect weather exposure, crosswinds and occasional traffic near towns and ports.

title: TR01 — Adriatic and Bosnia Seven-Day Grand Tour
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Croatia

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Banja Luka and head toward Una National Park and Štrbački Buk, where the road mixes forest sections, river views and quieter inland riding. This is a good warm-up for the Balkan terrain that follows. 
Road quality is variable on smaller sections, and village traffic is common. If you are close to the Bosnia–Croatia border, keep an eye on documentation and local road restrictions, especially around remote river roads.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride past the abandoned Željava Air Base and into Croatia toward Plitvice Lakes. The route becomes greener and more structured, with forest roads, lakes and smoother touring sections. 
Continue to Senj as the Adriatic approaches. The road begins to feel more coastal and open, though wind and occasional tourist traffic can be significant near the sea.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Ride the Adriatic coastal road past Karlobag toward Zadar. This is a classic Croatian motorcycle day: sea on one side, mountains on the other, and a long string of bends that reward a steady pace. 
Traffic can be busy in summer, and bora winds can make the exposed sections demanding. The road surface is generally good, but you should expect coaches, camper vans and frequent viewpoint stops.

title: HR02 — Hidden Istria Hill Towns Loop
subtitle: A 2-day tour of Croatia

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Pula and head inland into Istria’s hill country. The roads rise through vineyards and stone villages, with smooth but narrow asphalt and a steady sequence of short curves. 
Visit Motovun, Grožnjan and Buzet before stopping for the night. This is a culturally rich, low-speed day that fits the hidden-Istria character very well.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride through Hum and Kotli before climbing into the Učka mountains. The route gets steeper and more exposed, with a stronger mountain feel near Poklon Pass. 
The descent side offers long views toward the Adriatic. Surface quality is usually good, but forested sections can be damp and traffic can increase near the coast.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Corte and ride through Scala di Santa Regina toward Calacuccia and Col de Vergio. The road is narrow and deeply scenic, with gorge walls, forests and a constant sense of remoteness. 
Expect limited passing space, variable pavement and weather that can turn quickly in the mountains. The route is spectacular but demands patience and concentration on the tighter sections.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Move east across Corsica through Ghisoni and the Inzecca gorge before heading to Zicavo. The riding is technical, with narrow roads, repeated bends and strong mountain character. 
Road surfaces are generally acceptable, but the terrain is rugged and tourist traffic can appear around the best-known scenic points. The landscape is more important than the pace here.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Finish by climbing toward Zonza and Col de Bavella, where the famous granite spires dominate the skyline. The last day is short but powerful, with steep mountain roads and dramatic scenery. 
Weather can shift quickly at altitude, and loose gravel is possible near the edges of the road. This is one of Corsica’s signature motorcycle finales and an appropriate ending to the route.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Lesko and loop past Solina before heading deeper into the Bieszczady Mountains. The roads are quiet and forested, with gentle climbs and long bends that suit a relaxed touring rhythm. 
Continue through Cisna and Wetlina. The route is scenic but remote, and the forest edges can feel close to the road, especially where wildlife may emerge unexpectedly.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride east toward Ustrzyki Górne, then continue through Lutowiska and Czarna Górna. This is the quietest and most remote day of the loop, with very little traffic and a strong wilderness feel. 
Roads are generally in good condition, but they can be narrow and are often shared with animals, tractors and local traffic. Stay alert for deer and other wildlife, especially in the evening.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Return to Lesko on a shorter final stage that keeps the route realistic after two longer mountain days. The road is less demanding than the forest sections earlier in the trip, but it still offers a pleasant rolling finish. 
This closing day is mainly a practical transfer, though the Bieszczady scenery remains attractive throughout. It is a good final stretch before leaving southeastern Poland.

title: CZ01 — Bohemian Switzerland Rock Roads Loop
subtitle: A 2-day tour of Czech Republic

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Start in Děčín and ride along the Elbe toward Hřensko and Janov, where sandstone walls and forested hills define the landscape. Continue through Srbská Kamenice, Jetřichovice and Chřibská before reaching Doubice, Kyjov and Krásná Lípa. 
The roads are narrow, winding and scenic, with frequent shaded sections and occasional damp surfaces. Traffic can increase around popular hiking areas, while blind bends, cyclists and local vehicles require a controlled pace.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Continue from Krásná Lípa through Jiřetín pod Jedlovou, Krompach and Jablonné v Podještědí. The mandatory stop is Pekelné Doly, the famous biker cave bar where motorcycles can enter the former sandstone mining complex. 
After Pekelné Doly, ride through Česká Kamenice and return to Děčín. The second day combines forest roads, sandstone formations and small Bohemian towns, with generally good pavement but occasional patched sections and slow village passages.

title: IBR01 — Douro Valley to Arribes Border Ride
subtitle: A 3-day tour of Portugal

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Ride the N222 from Peso da Régua to Pinhão and onward through the Douro vineyards. The road is famous for its flowing bends and river views, with terraced hillsides on both sides. 
Traffic is usually moderate, but the road can be slower than it looks because of viewpoints, trucks and agricultural activity. It is best ridden with a relaxed pace and plenty of time for stops.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Head east through the Douro Internacional toward Freixo de Espada à Cinta and Miranda do Douro. The scenery changes from vineyards to a much more rugged canyon landscape, with quiet roads and fewer services. 
The route is smoother than the mountain roads farther north, but it still feels remote. Cross-border movement into Spain requires normal travel documents, though formal checks are generally minimal within Schengen.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Continue through Arribes del Duero into Spain, where the route stays close to the canyon rim and the roads are light on traffic. The final stretch into Salamanca is more straightforward, but the landscape remains attractive. 
This is a well-balanced final day, suitable for finishing a border route without overloading the rider. Surface quality is good overall, though rural debris and tight village corners can appear.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Cangas del Narcea and head into Somiedo on roads that drop into green valleys and climb back into remote mountain country. The riding is scenic and lightly trafficked, with forests coming close to the asphalt in many sections. 
Expect wildlife, especially at dawn and dusk, and a generally quiet pace away from the villages. The route is not technically extreme, but it feels wild and isolated.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Climb from Valle de Lago toward Puerto de San Lorenzo and then continue to Puerto de Ventana. This is the route’s high-point day, with mountain passes, open views and a stronger sense of elevation. 
The roads are generally good, but fog and rain can appear suddenly in Asturias. Keep a conservative pace through the tighter bends and shaded forest sections.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Use the last day as a short transfer back to Oviedo. The road is less demanding than the previous two stages, but it still offers a pleasant final run through the Asturias hills. 
This final stretch is practical rather than spectacular, which helps the route stay realistic after the more remote mountain riding. Weather and traffic can change quickly as you approach the city.

days.title: Day 1
days.description:
Leave Røldal and cross Saudafjellet on Fv520, a remote high road that can hold snow into the warmer months. The scenery is open and wild, with long views and very little traffic. 
Descend toward Sauda past Allmannajuvet and Svandalsfossen, then continue to Sand. The route is scenic and isolated, but weather changes quickly and fuel stops should not be skipped.

days.title: Day 2
days.description:
Ride along the Ryfylke fjords toward Hjelmeland and the Songesand ferry terminal. This stage mixes water-level roads with narrow fjord corridors and occasional ferry-dependent routing. 
The ferry crossing into the Lysefjord system is a core part of the route and should be planned around the timetable. Once you reach Lysebotn, the terrain becomes more dramatic and more technical.

days.title: Day 3
days.description:
Climb Lysevegen’s famous hairpins out of Lysebotn, then descend toward Stavanger. The road is steep, narrow and visually spectacular, with tight corners and tunnel sections that require careful speed management. 
The final run is a strong closing stage, but it is shorter than the first two days. Expect changing weather, limited overtaking room and a high concentration of scenic viewpoints.
